newsitem.title: GERMANY: German trade surplus hits 10.4 bln DM in April.
newsitem.headline: German trade surplus hits 10.4 bln DM in April.

text.p: Germany's trade surplus grew to 10.4 billion marks ($6 billion) in April from 9.8 billion marks the previous month, the Federal Statistics Office reported.
The surplus is also up from 7.7 billion marks in April 1996.

The current account, the broadest measure of trade including services, was in surplus by 2.8 billion marks in April, compared with a 2.9 billion mark surplus in March and a 1.3 billion mark deficit in the year-earlier month.

Exports in April were 73.4 billion marks, up from 70.4 billion marks and 65.3 billion marks, respectively, while imports rose to 63.0 billion marks from 60.6 billion marks in March and 57.6 billion marks a year earlier.

For the first four months of 1997, the trade surplus was 34.7 billion marks, up from 26.8 billion marks a year earlier, while the current account was in deficit by 5.9 billion marks, growing from a 2.8 billion mark gap in the same period of 1996.
Exports in the four months totalled 276.0 billion marks, up from 254.5 billion marks, while imports were 241.3 billion marks, up from 227.7 billion marks. ($ = 1.726 German Marks)
